Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll read `README.md` first as required, then use the fish-control bookshelf and wake-visual inspection skills before proposing or editing the single candidate. I’ll keep the candidate rationale in the required notes and extract one evidence-backed reusable lesson into the shared guidance.

The workspace confirms that only the target policy is editable under `solver/`, CFD must not be run here, and the prefilled parent is `solver_a763085dcb98`. I’m now applying the two required skills: the bookshelf skill will constrain any mechanism transfer to body-frame invariants, and the visual-first skill will determine which wake evidence must be inspected before changing the policy.

The inherited guidance already identifies a specific failure pattern: distance/proximity-based relief fired during useful closure, while permanent full drive overshot after a strong approach. I’m now comparing the four completed descendants—not just their scores—to identify whether closure gating, steering topology, or carrier behavior caused the semantic regression.

The inherited log adds a decisive completed result missing from the current durable guidance: half-cycle posterior asymmetry recovered a strong `3.259L` approach, but still exited high and receded to `7.016L`. That suggests it preserved thrust better than scalar relief yet did not fix late course conversion. I’m inspecting the paired top-down/oblique sheets now to verify whether wake coherence and exit topology support that reading.

The sheets confirm direct self-propulsion and coherent alternating 3D wakes across all variants; none fails from wake collapse. The inherited half-cycle policy visibly produces a much sharper late bend, but only after its path has already passed above the target. I’m consulting the bookshelf references now for a mechanism that advances route response without merely retuning a gain or damping the carrier.

The bookshelf points to changing the actuator/feedback primitive when repeated scalar edits preserve the same failure topology. That matches the evidence: scalar relief, damping, closure gating, and late half-cycle asymmetry all leave an upper exit. I’m reconstructing normalized bearing, course error, yaw response, and actuator residence from the saved trajectories so the next mechanism’s sign and activation window are evidence-calibrated.

The trajectory reconstruction supports one focused hypothesis: use the already effective posterior half-cycle asymmetry earlier only when body-frame bearing and target-versus-velocity course error agree in sign. On the inherited half-cycle history, this gate is off at the misleading `4T` bearing/course disagreement, engages during the coherent miss at roughly `8T`, and releases when course alignment returns—so it is a response-triggered redirect, not a distance or clock schedule. I’m recording that diagnosis before touching the policy, as required.

The pre-edit provenance is now in place. I’m implementing exactly one candidate: the inherited full carrier plus response-gated posterior half-cycle redirection. The only new controller mechanism is the agreement gate; proximity remains solely for the already evidenced small anterior course redistribution, not for propulsion relief.

The single candidate is implemented and remains non-empty. Its posterior asymmetry is now self-releasing on course alignment and inactive on bearing/course disagreement; no new coordinate, clock, route memory, or scalar carrier damping was added. I’m distilling the completed inherited half-cycle result into the reusable experience bank before validation.

Both required files now contain substantive updates, and the candidate owns every new active parameter. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the configured check runner for deterministic policy, schema, reflection, and guidance validation; it will not run CFD or edit the candidate.
The first invocation was rejected because configured checker agents cannot inherit full conversation history. I’m retrying it with the workspace path and validation scope stated explicitly.

The configured checker could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this environment. I’ll complete the same non-CFD checklist locally from the checker specification, including a contract evaluation if Julia is available, and repair any deterministic failure before finishing.

The guidance checker found a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` marks the same optimizer parent as copied twice, so the assigned parent is not uniquely resolvable. This is the same deterministic issue documented in inherited runs. I’m removing only the duplicate marker, then rerunning the check.

The repaired guidance check passes, and the repository boundary check passes. Julia is not installed here, so I’m replacing only that unavailable runtime assertion with deterministic schema, source-structure, finite-output, and mirror-equivariance checks against the same policy algebra; CFD remains untouched.

All available non-CFD checks now pass: guidance semantics, editable boundary, one non-empty policy, 23/23 parameter ownership, finite two-joint outputs, and 1,001 mirror-equivariance cases. I’m doing the final artifact/count check and then I’ll hand off the candidate without running formal CFD.

Produced exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) adds response-gated posterior half-cycle redirection when bearing and course error agree.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, audit, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:96) now captures the inherited half-cycle result and its proximity-scheduling failure.

Guidance and boundary checks pass, all 23 parameter references are owned, and finite-output/reflection checks passed across 1,001 cases. The configured checker model and Julia were unavailable, so equivalent deterministic checks were run locally. No CFD was run.
